doc.title: Carmen Lundy interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 15, 2023

title: Singing six nights a week in Miami: Pirate's Cove and the Eden Roc
summary: She worked nightly gigs through university, starting with the band Shadow and then a year at the Eden Roc with Roitstein.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: I’m guessing that accompanists, bass players and piano players and guitar players like to work with you because I doubt you would ever call a tune that you didn’t know your own key or have a chart on or an arrangement idea.

Absolutely. So when I moved to New York it was the late 70s, okay? And there was a preparation for that. I was, during my years at the University of Miami I sang six nights a week, three sets 9:00 to 1:00 in any venue that would hire me. Most of the gigs, back then when you booked a gig it lasted for a year, or it lasted for at least, at a minimum a month and then some other artist would come in and then you’d come back in in a month, you know two months later and it was like that sort of thing. So the way I kind of provided for myself during my university years was singing every night in Miami somewhere. My first full time, a full year, my very first employment was at the Eden Roc Hotel in Miami Beach. Prior to that the very first gig it didn’t last a year but it lasted a full summer going into that year and that gig was on North Miami Beach at a place called the Pirate’s Cove and the group was called Shadow, and I was the shadow. And okay, so that was the summer. So it was like cool, you didn’t have to get up and make the 8:30 theory class in the summer. But when I got that gig at the Eden Roc, that gig lasted for a year.
